what_it_does: When you have a back-and-forth conversation with an AI assistant, the model has to remember everything said earlier in the chat. Internally it keeps a running record of 'keys and values' — a data structure (called KV cache) that encodes all prior turns — so that new words can attend to what came before. Current serving systems throw away this record after each response and rebuild it from scratch on the next question, wasting significant computation by reprocessing text the model has already seen. This paper proposes keeping that record alive across turns so the model can simply pick up where it left off, eliminating redundant work. It also redesigns the scheduling policy that decides which incoming requests to serve next: instead of a simple first-come-first-served queue (which lets a very long accumulated conversation hog the GPU and delay everyone else), it reorders or briefly pauses requests based on how much context they carry, keeping the hardware more evenly loaded.
